name: Naturalisation via Marriage to a Sudanese Man

requirements.blocker_text: Applicant must be a foreign woman married to a Sudanese national man -- no equivalent route for a foreign man married to a Sudanese woman was located in this build.
2 years' residence with the Sudanese spouse (waivable at Presidential discretion for a person with prior qualifying residency).
requirements.fix_path: Reside with the Sudanese spouse for 2 years before applying.

evidence_required.document: Proof of 2 years' cohabitation/residence with the spouse

outcome.physical_presence_requirement: 2 years' residence with the Sudanese spouse

sources.title: Citizenship Rights in Africa Initiative -- Sudanese Nationality Act 1994, as amended: 'Foreign women married to Sudanese nationals may obtain naturalization upon demonstrating two years' residence with their spouse' -- a preferential fast-track compared to the ordinary 10-year naturalisation residence requirement; Presidential discretion may waive the 2-year requirement for a person with prior qualifying residency

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Sudan). STATUS: DRAFT -- same tier-2-only sourcing limitation as sd_citizenship_naturalisation.json (NGO-hosted consolidated translation; no tier-1 Sudanese-government copy located). MARQUEE GENDERED FINDING, CONSISTENT WITH A PATTERN SEEN REPEATEDLY IN THIS DATASET (Qatar, Bahrain, Nigeria): the sourced text frames this fast-track marriage-naturalisation route around a FOREIGN WOMAN married to a Sudanese MAN -- no search conducted in this build located any equivalent provision for a foreign man married to a Sudanese woman, who would instead be limited to the ordinary 10-year naturalisation track (sd_citizenship_naturalisation.json) or the Presidential-discretion clause, neither of which offers the same fast-track. This is disclosed as a confirmed structural asymmetry based on the sourced text's own framing, not an inference. dual_citizenship_allowed FALSE, consistent with sd_citizenship_naturalisation.json's notes on the Act's general non-recognition of dual citizenship (with the specific South Sudan automatic-revocation rule as an added, distinct mechanism).
